newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to March 14.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to March 14.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a sharp 21.95 percent decline in turnover during the week ending March 14 amidst tightening liquidity.
Total turnover fell to 26.897 million dinars ($4.77 million) in 189 transactions, from 34.46 million dinars in 213 deals a week ago.
Traders saw no particular reason for the declining activity apart from deterioration of the overall financial situation.
"Whenever the government has to pay pensions or wages to state employees, the money disappears from this market," a trader told Reuters.
Some traders said banks and companies had withdrawn funds to settle old debts.
Analysts saw the decline in BSE turnover resulting from the latest decision by the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) to technically update the 15 percent reserve requirement.
Commercial banks initially fulfilled the reserve requirement by transferring 15 percent of their deposits but are now obliged to also deposit with the NBY 15 percent of money lent to other banks.
Traders complained that the measures, aimed at restoring financial discipline, destroyed the most lucrative part of the financial market.
"Bank-to-bank lending was always less risky than any lending to the companies sector. Banks pay back, companies don't," said the analyst who asked not to be named.
But analysts agreed the central bank had effectively achieved what it wanted, with money increasingly going to the companies sector.
For the week ending March 14, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 171 transactions totalling 23.807 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded 10 times for a volume of 0.94 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent. Maturity ran between five and 30 days.
* There was only one deal in central bank short-term bonds. The NBY sold 0.3 million dinars worth of bonds at its auction last Friday.
* The bourse reported five deals in wheat contracts worth 1.5 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills inched up to 22.789 million dinars from 22.103 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading surplus liquidity, remained almost unchanged at 13.5 million dinars against 13.27 million a week ago.
-- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
($1 = 5.6334 Yugoslav dinars)
